ribbons.text: I walked my round that night. Same as any night.
ribbons.press_text: 'Needle Lane, Cutter's Row, back along the wall. Forty-one lamps. I have walked it eleven years.'

ribbons.text: The Chandlers had no business on my streets.
ribbons.press_text: 'Their wax, their carts, their little sealed dockets. Business, they call it. We call it Tuesday.'

ribbons.text: Every lamp on the lane was burning when I left it.
ribbons.press_text: 'Burning. I do not leave a lamp guttering. Ask anyone. Ask the lamps.'

ribbons.text: And it was signed for, same as any round.
ribbons.press_text: 'Signed and countersigned. The Chandlers pay for the oil, so the Chandlers get their signature.'
ribbons.break_text: Merrow goes still. 'That is Wick's hand. And that is the night nobody signed.' She fetches the tally without being asked.
ribbons.rebuff_text: 'That proves nothing about my round, cat.'

when_outcome.success: The thread that would not hold, caught. Merrow respects it, which is worse than liking it.
when_outcome.partial: Merrow stops talking. Not angry — done. The lane will be colder next time.
when_outcome.walk_away: Ash lets it lie. The Lamplighters keep their tally and their opinions.

ribbons.text: Needle Lane was empty that night. Nothing to see. Nothing to sell you.
ribbons.press_text: 'Empty. Quiet as a church and half as honest. My people had no business there, and saw nobody having any either.'

ribbons.text: The lamps went out on their own. Old wicks, wet air. Nothing in it.
ribbons.press_text: 'Forty-one lamps, all tired at the same minute.' He watches me while he says it. He is not lying to me; he is seeing whether I will do the work.

ribbons.text: We came off the lane at the ninth hour. Standard practice, that.
ribbons.press_text: 'Standard practice when a cart is coming and not slowing. You do not stand about in front of that.' He hears it as he says it, and does not take it back -- rats never take it back, they wait to be charged for it.

ribbons.text: Nothing came down that lane but weather.
ribbons.press_text: 'Weather and dark and my people's own good sense. That is the whole of it.'
ribbons.break_text: I put the stub down on his ledger, seal up. Beeswax, guild-marked, found under a window on a street where nothing came but weather. 'Weather does not deliver candles,' I say. The Grey Boss looks at it a long moment and stops performing. 'All right, cat. All right. There was a cart -- Chandlers' cart, no chandler on it. And a gentleman walking behind it who did not walk like a man going anywhere.'
ribbons.rebuff_text: 'A candle end. My mother could do better than a candle end.'

when_outcome.success: He gives me the cart, the hour, and a man with no destination. Rats charge for their memory, and this one has just been paid.
when_outcome.partial: He gives me the shape of it and keeps the corners. Rats do not lie. They invoice.
when_outcome.walk_away: I leave him his story intact. It will cost more next time, and he knows that I know.
